current_episode.title: EP 280 The Fastest Way to Build a Profitable Retreat Business with Shari Leid

guest.titre: Attorney, Author, Speaker, and Retreat Leader
guest.bio_context: Shari Leid is an attorney by training who later stayed home to raise her kids and began writing, publishing her first book; her fifth book is due in February. She built a portfolio career spanning writing, media contributions, speaking, and most recently retreats, centered on a framework called FLIP (Flip the Box), born from a 2023 cross-country journey where she shared a meal with a female stranger in every U.S. state. Her personal backstory — being orphaned and found in a cardboard box with no known birth date or identifying information — directly inspired her work on human connection and belonging.

context.real_quote: A lot of us have a good life, but if we don't feel connected, we're letting that good life stop us from a great life.

pending_qa.q: What approach did Shari Leid take before launching her first retreat to avoid costly mistakes?
pending_qa.r: Before her first retreat, Shari proactively sought out expert guidance, reaching out to retreat strategist Shannon Jamal for a one-on-one coaching session. She explained her philosophy as 'start ugly and make it pretty as you go along,' prioritizing learning from experienced practitioners over figuring everything out independently.

pending_qa.q: What two business model additions does Shannon Jamal recommend as the most powerful revenue legs for coaches and speakers?
pending_qa.r: Shannon Jamal argues that a membership program generating recurring revenue and in-person retreat experiences are the two most powerful legs a coach, speaker, or online expert can add to their business right now. She specifically highlights that as the world becomes increasingly digital and AI-driven, people are craving in-person experiences across virtually every topic.

pending_qa.q: What is Shari Leid's free FLIP app and what does it do?
pending_qa.r: Shari Leid offers a free FLIP app on her website that walks users through the four steps of her connection framework after a conversation. The app diagnoses where a person may be losing connection — whether through lack of focus, poor listening, slipping into control mode, or playing small.

pending_qa.q: What key insight did Shari Leid take away from attending the Retreat Leaders Forum in Denver?
pending_qa.r: At the Denver forum, Shari observed that retreat leaders at all levels do things very differently, and that there is no single cookie-cutter approach to running a successful retreat business. She learned to selectively adopt strategies that fit her own personality and model, rather than trying to replicate someone else's exact system.

pending_qa.q: What role does messaging play in filling a retreat, according to the conversation between Shari Leid and Shannon Jamal?
pending_qa.r: Shannon Jamal emphasized that nail-tight messaging — clearly identifying who the retreat is for and what problem it solves — is the single most important element before worrying about platforms or tactics. As evidence, Shari shared that a woman in her early 70s booked her retreat without ever speaking to Shari first, trusting entirely on the clarity and resonance of Shari's messaging and brand.
